papers.title: Boat-racing programme
lines: Anguillan sloops race on holidays, sails wild and crews wilder. Each boat is named for a sweetheart, a saint or a boast.
Whoever wins, the party goes on till the rum is gone and then continues without it.

papers.title: Salt pond note
lines: Salt pond at Sandy Ground: the old work of the island, now a quiet pink pool and a dozen birds.
I sat and counted them. The count was the same as last year. The birds seemed to approve.

trail.clue: A fisherman's catch tin of coins lies near the open ground, 'out of the wind'.

papers.title: Postcard from Anguilla
lines: Greetings from a thirty-mile coral island with sea the colour of a toothpaste advert.
I have eaten lobster on the beach. I have eaten lobster at the bar. I have lobster-based plans.

papers.title: Letter from a nephew
lines: Dear Auntie, the sun is fierce and the music is sweeter. I am learning to sail a sloop and to lose a race gracefully.
Send biscuits. The humidity ate mine.
